title: Contracts, Amendments & Renewals

toc.text: Contract statuses and the agreement lifecycle
Amendments: changing an agreement without breaking it
Hands-on walkthrough: generate a contract and automate a renewal

html:
Quotes capture intent; contracts capture obligation. Contracts, Amendments & Renewals is the phase where the approved quote becomes a legally usable agreement, where mid-term changes become amendments, and where the recurring revenue you priced gets a second (and third) life through renewals. It carries 15% of the Certified CPQ Specialist blueprint — the highest-scoring downstream domain alongside Orders — and it is where the academy data model gets its Contract fields, the Renewal_Opportunity__c object, and the ContractGenerationService and RenewalQuoteService Apex services.

This guide explains how contracts are born from quotes, how amendments keep the master agreement accurate, and how renewals — including co-termination and uplift — turn a single sale into a revenue stream.

Learning objectives

  • Describe how a contract is generated from an approved, contracted quote and which fields carry over.
  • Track contract status and key contractual dates with CPQ_Contract_Status__c.
  • Generate contracts programmatically with ContractGenerationService.
  • Use amendments to modify contracts after signing while preserving the original terms.
  • Configure automatic renewal options via Auto_Renew__c and Renewal_Term_Months__c.
  • Build renewal opportunities on Renewal_Opportunity__c and manage co-termination.
  • Apply renewal uplift with Uplift_Percent__c and RenewalQuoteService.
  • Connect contracts to orders and to the billing engine for the rest of the lifecycle.

From quote to contract

The contract is generated from the quote at the moment the deal is commercialized. CPQ does not re-negotiate: it transfers the agreed lines, quantities, prices, term, and discount from the quote onto a contract and its line items. The gate is that only a quote in an approved (and optionally e-signed) state can generate a contract — the same gate approval logic enforces.

On the academy model the contract carries the key commercial signals:

Contract fieldMeaningTypical source
ARR__cAnnual recurring value of the agreementSum of line ARR from the quote
Auto_Renew__cWhether the contract renews without a new signatureQuote / product family setting
Renewal_Term_Months__cTerm applied at renewalProduct default or negotiation
Uplift_Percent__cPrice increase applied at renewalRenewal policy
CPQ_Contract_Status__cLifecycle state: Draft/Pending/Mastered/ExpiredStatus field
apex
// ContractGenerationService: create a contract shell from an approved quote
public class ContractGenerationService {
    public static Contract create(Quote quote) {
        if (quote.Approval_Status__c != 'Approved') {
            throw new CalloutException('Cannot generate a contract from an unapproved quote.');
        }
        return new Contract(
            Name                 = quote.Name + ' - Contract',
            ContractTerm         = Integer.valueOf(quote.Contract_Term_Months__c),
            ARR__c               = quote.Total_ARR__c,
            Auto_Renew__c        = true,
            Renewal_Term_Months__c = 12,
            CPQ_Contract_Status__c = 'Pending'
        );
    }
}
💡
Tip: The contract must have an activated status before downstream order or subscription automation trusts it. Keep CPQ_Contract_Status__c moving deliberately: Draft → Pending → Mastered → (Amended | Renewed | Expired).

Contract statuses and the agreement lifecycle

A contract is not one static record; it has a lifecycle. In legacy CPQ the admin acts on the contract and the package tracks its state — created, sent to customer, signed/executed, actually (mastered) effective, and later expired or renewed. Because the academy model exposes status on CPQ_Contract_Status__c, your automations can branch on it confidently:

soql
SELECT Id, Name, CPQ_Contract_Status__c, ARR__c, Auto_Renew__c,
       Renewal_Term_Months__c, Uplift_Percent__c, ContractTerm,
       StartDate, EndDate
FROM Contract
ORDER BY StartDate DESC

Status values are your process contract: an orchestration layer (you will build one in the Orders & Fulfillment phase) decides which actions are legal in each state. Never let an integration edit a Mastered contract directly — true changes go through amendments.

Amendments: changing an agreement without breaking it

An amendment is a change order against a mastered contract. Pricing, quantities, contract term, product mix — anything can change mid-term, but the original contract document must stay intact as the legal baseline. The amendment records the delta and, once executed, becomes the new effective terms.

ChangeAmendment impact
Add licenses mid-termProrated new line, adjusted total
Remove a moduleCredit / term adjustment
Extend termEndDate moves, renewal dates shift
Discount change or uplift correctionUnit prices adjusted on the affected lines

Amendments matter for revenue work because they change recognition inputs: a small amendment to quantity on a subscription ripples into the billing schedule, the revenue schedule, and the next renewal's starting point. That is why contract status must remain Mastered — the amendment is the sanctioned mutation path, and every downstream object should key off the amended terms, not the original snapshot.

The renewal machine: Renewal_Opportunity__c

Renewals are where recurring-revenue businesses prove their model. CPQ generates a renewal opportunity from a contract before its term ends, bundling the expiring lines into a renewal quote. In the academy model, Renewal_Opportunity__c is the bridge record:

FieldPurpose
Account__cRenewing customer
Contract__cSource agreement
Renewal_Date__cWhen the renewal should close/start
ARR__cProjected renewal value
Uplift_Percent__cContractual or policy uplift to apply
Status__cOpen / Generated / Won / Lost

The renewal process reads the contract's lines, applies Renewal_Term_Months__c and Uplift_Percent__c, and calls RenewalQuoteService to produce a renewal quote that reps can adjust and discount exactly like new business — with full approval, document, and contracting support.

apex
// RenewalQuoteService: stage the renewal opportunity from a mastered contract
public class RenewalQuoteService {
    public static Renewal_Opportunity__c stage(Contract master) {
        return new Renewal_Opportunity__c(
            Account__c        = master.AccountId,
            Contract__c       = master.Id,
            Renewal_Date__c   = master.EndDate.addMonths(-90),
            ARR__c            = master.ARR__c,
            Uplift_Percent__c = master.Uplift_Percent__c == null ? 5 : master.Uplift_Percent__c,
            Status__c         = 'Open'
        );
    }
}
💡
Tip: Set renewal dates back from the term end (commonly 90 days) so reps have a full quarter to negotiate — a renewal surfaced 10 days before expiry is usually already lost.

Co-termination

Co-termination is the policy that pulls every agreement for one customer onto a single renewal date. It massively simplifies account management — one renewal conversation, one contract, one set of dates — at the cost of prorating the pipes between now and the unified date.

ApproachEffect
No co-terminationEach contract renews on its own anniversary
Co-termination on masterAll renew on the master agreement's date
Co-termination per accountAll of an account's agreements renew together

The math is the tricky part: shorter-term contracts whose anniversary is inside the co-term window get realigned, and value from the removed quarter(s) is typically credited or folded into the renewal uplift. Revenue Cloud / RLM models this as part of asset lifecycle management: assets (not just contracts) carry the subscription records that get grouped for renewal.

Uplift, discounts, and renewal economics

Renewal uplift is the CPR of the subscription model: a 5% uplift on a 5-year customer compounds into a big ARR number with no new logo required. The academy model puts the policy on the contract (Uplift_Percent__c) and the intent on the renewal opportunity, while the renewal quote carries Is_Renewal__c = true and Uplift_Percent__c on the Quote so downstream reporting can separate renewal from net-new ARR.

text
Renewal ARR output = Sum(line ARR on renewal quote)
Renewal uplift $   = Renewal ARR - (contract ARR at prior renewal)

Guard the discount: an uplift policy that routinely gets negotiated back to zero on Renewal_Opportunity__c is a leakage signal — exactly the pattern your Analytics & Revenue Reporting phase will flag with Discount_Leakage_Percent__c on the opportunity.

Hands-on walkthrough: generate a contract and automate a renewal

This walkthrough uses the academy data model plus ContractGenerationService and RenewalQuoteService.

  1. Confirm you have an approved quote with Total_ARR__c, Contract_Term_Months__c, and Approval_Status__c = 'Approved'.
  2. Generate the contract from the quote:
apex
Contract c = ContractGenerationService.create(approvedQuote);
insert c;
  1. Activate the contract: set CPQ_Contract_Status__c = 'Mastered', set StartDate, and let EndDate compute from ContractTerm. Confirm ARR__c equals the quote's Total_ARR__c.
  2. Stage the renewal opportunity:
apex
Renewal_Opportunity__c ro = RenewalQuoteService.stage(c);
insert ro;
  1. Change the contract's Uplift_Percent__c to 5, then call RenewalQuoteService again and confirm the renewal quote's Quote record now has Is_Renewal__c = true and Uplift_Percent__c = 5.
  2. Simulate co-termination: set the second contract's renewal date equal to the master's via SOQL update, then run the renewal staging and verify both renewals land on the same Renewal_Date__c.
soql
SELECT Id, Contract__c, Renewal_Date__c, ARR__c, Uplift_Percent__c, Status__c
FROM Renewal_Opportunity__c
ORDER BY Renewal_Date__c
  1. Create an amendment that adds a module mid-term: insert an amended line, recalc, and confirm the contract remains Mastered while a delta is recorded.
  2. Verify the contract's fields feed the billing engine: the Contract__c link on Revenue_Schedule__c exists so recognition follows the amended terms, not the original snapshot.

Common pitfalls

  • Generating contracts from unapproved quotes — without the approval gate your contracts carry pricing nobody signed off; always guard in ContractGenerationService.
  • Editing a mastered contract directly — mutation must go through amendments or the legal baseline and the revenue records drift apart.
  • Renewals surfaced too late — staging renewal at expiry guarantees rushed, under-negotiated renewals; stage 90+ days out.
  • Ignoring co-termination math — realigning dates without prorating value shows up later as billing disputes and cancelled lines.
  • Uplift treated as a suggestion — if renewal reps routinely zero the uplift, enforce it in pricing rules and report the leakage.
  • Forgetting what carries the ARR — the contract is a snapshot; the recurring value lives on the lines and assets that feed orders and billing.

Key takeaways

  • Contracts are generated from approved quotes and gate the entire downstream (orders, billing, revenue recognition).
  • The contract lifecycle (Draft → Mastered → Amended/Renewed → Expired) is a process contract your automations must respect.
  • Amendments record deltas against an intact master so legal and revenue records stay truthful.
  • Renewals turn one sale into a stream: stage Renewal_Opportunity__c early, apply uplift deliberately, and co-terminate with prorated math when unifying dates.
  • Every downstream object keys off the contract's amended terms — the renewal is only as good as the source agreement's accuracy.
